newsitem.title: USA: Sears sees higher Xmas sales than last year.
newsitem.headline: Sears sees higher Xmas sales than last year.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck & Co said it expects sales during this holiday season to surpass last year's as people buy up everything from tools to underwear to winter tyres at its department stores throughout the United States.
"Sales are forecast to top 1995's solid holiday performance," said John Costello, senior executive-vice president of marketing.
Costello said in an interview on Sunday that the company would release figures for December sales on January 16.
Sears reported $4.36 billion in total store revenues for the five weeks ended December 31, 1995, up 9.2 percent from the same period the previous year, according to a company spokeswoman.
Costello said Sears began advertising a week before the Christmas shopping season officially began.
He said it decided to launch a seasonal sale one week before Thanksgiving since there were five fewer days to the holiday season.
This year's success was also partly the result of a remodelling of its stores and a realignment of its market that Sears began in 1993, he added.
